findings.disposition: future-caller risk, not a current bug — no current caller triggers this path
findings.summary: Empty-state branch renders the Add button without a `disabled` prop; non-empty branch hides it when disabled=true — asymmetric behaviour across the two render paths
findings.failure_scenario: A future caller that passes disabled=true with a non-empty list and then clears the list (e.g. after a failed refresh) would see the Add button appear even though disabled=true. No current caller reaches this path: the only passer of disabled=true is IntegrationSection with disabled={isRequired && hasNoSettings}, and hasNoSettings=false whenever the list is non-empty.

findings.disposition: pre-existing, out of scope for this fix
findings.summary: Dead sub-conditions: `!selectOptions` and `!settingsDefinitions` are always false
findings.failure_scenario: settingsDefinitions is coerced to [] on line 60 (never null/undefined); selectOptions is derived via .map() (always an array). Both guards are unreachable — the condition reduces to settingsDefinitions.length === 0. No bug, but the dead checks mask intent and could mislead future readers.

findings.disposition: pre-existing, out of scope for this fix
findings.summary: disabled={isRequired && hasNoSettings} is now a no-op after this fix
findings.failure_scenario: When hasNoSettings=true the empty-state branch in IntegrationSelectDropdown fires regardless of disabled. When hasNoSettings=false, disabled evaluates to false anyway. The prop has no observable effect with any current caller. Future maintainers may be confused about its purpose. Cleanup opportunity: remove or rename the prop to reflect its true intent.

summary: Fix correctly removes the !disabled guard that was suppressing the Add User Integration button for all required-integration datasource types when no integrations were configured. All three acceptance criteria pass. Three pre-existing notes surfaced (asymmetric disabled handling, dead conditions, no-op disabled prop in IntegrationSection) — none blocking, none introduced by this diff. Approved.
